correctness.rationale: For each odd m, m reflection cut classes each have q^((m+1)/2) words; primitive classes are disjoint, and nonprimitive words have divisor period at most m/3. This yields Omega_q(m q^(m/2)) language members. A direct second-moment calculation with overlapping matches yields uniform lower appearance probability mu/(mu+1+2/(q-1)). Sum the geometric upper bound over all lengths and restrict the lower bound to the largest odd m<=floor(log_q N). The finite verifier passes and the symbolic estimates handle every N sufficiently large.

value.rationale: A natural refinement of probabilistic palindromic richness exhibits a genuinely different logarithmically enhanced growth law, explained by primitive two-palindrome cut multiplicity. This applies to all fixed q>=2, all large N, and is not just a narrow finite count or repetition of Kemp's language census.
